Submission Checklist

This checklist is a preparation guide only. Always verify your submission requirements and deadlines directly with RICS. Get Chartered AI is not responsible for submission compliance or deadline management.

📝 Case Study Review — Michael's Coaching

Paste your case study draft below. Michael will review it and give you specific coaching feedback.

RICS Case Study Requirements

Your case study is strictly limited to 3,000 words maximum. This includes headings and subheadings but excludes the cover page, contents page and appendices.

The recommended structure is:

  • Introduction — approximately 400 words
  • Approach — approximately 1,000 words
  • Achievements — approximately 1,200 words
  • Conclusion — approximately 400 words

Source: RICS APC submissions and assessment guidance

This is AI-generated coaching feedback to help you develop your case study. It is not an official RICS assessment and does not predict your outcome. Always review feedback with your counsellor before submission. Get Chartered AI accepts no responsibility for APC submission outcomes.

Case Study Review

Your case study is likely to shape many of the questions you face at final assessment.

Upload your referral report and Michael will help turn the assessor feedback into a structured recovery plan. Review each comment, confirm what it means for your preparation, and identify the evidence, practice, or support you need before your resit.

Then use Michael to review your case study draft, identify areas that may attract follow-up questions, and strengthen how clearly you explain your decisions, advice, and professional judgement.

RICS Case Study Requirements

Your case study is strictly limited to 3,000 words maximum. This includes headings and subheadings but excludes the cover page, contents page and appendices.

The recommended structure is:

  • Introduction — approximately 400 words
  • Approach — approximately 1,000 words
  • Achievements — approximately 1,200 words
  • Conclusion — approximately 400 words

What Michael reviews

  • What is working well in your draft
  • What to strengthen before submission
  • Questions your assessor is likely to ask based on what you have written
  • One thing to discuss with your counsellor
Important: This is AI-generated coaching feedback to help you develop your case study. It is not an official RICS assessment and does not predict your outcome. Referral Recovery Plan
Your Referral Recovery Plan

Upload your referral report and Michael will help you turn the assessor feedback into a structured recovery plan. Review each comment, confirm what it means for your preparation, and identify the evidence, practice, or support you need before your resit.

Michael won't decide what the assessors meant on your behalf — referral reports are often brief or ambiguous, and you know your own situation better than any tool can. Instead, Michael proposes an interpretation for each comment, and you confirm, amend, or reject it before it becomes part of your plan.
